result.topic_en: Euler explains the use of the 'absolute parts' of the increment. When Z depends only on x and y, setting N = 0 solves the problem. When Z also involves p, q, r, ..., the Euler–Lagrange equation leaves arbitrary constants, and these are fixed by natural boundary conditions at x = a.

qua indefinite relatio inter $x$ et $y$ exprimeretur, reli-
quae vero incrementi partes absolutae, vtpote ad vlti-
mos tantum ipsius $y$ valores pertinentes, non in com-
putum venirent.

XXVI.

Neque tamen hae partes absolutae frustra
sunt inuentae, sed singularem praestant vsum, ad
quem methodus mea prior, quae tantum aequatio-
nem $N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-$ etc. $=0$ suppeditauit, minus est
accommodata; quam ob causam haec methodus illi
longe est anteferenda. Quem vsum quo clarius ex-
ponam, sit primo $Z$ functio tantum ipsarum $x$ et $y$,
earum differentialia non inuoluens, ita vt sit $dZ=Mdx$
$+Ndy$, existentibus $P=0$, $Q=0$, etc. ac mani-
festum est, hoc casu partes absolutas sponte euanescere,
atque adeo problema perfecte esse solutum, statim ac
fecerimus $N=0$. Ita si $(bb-nxy+\frac{y^3}{c})dx$ debeat
esse maximum vel minimum, ob $N=-nx+\frac{3yy}{c}$,
quaestioni satisfit, statuendo $yy=\frac{1}{3}ncx$, neque hic quic-
quam vltra determinandum superest.

XXVII.

At si $Z$ praeterea inuoluat $p=\frac{dy}{dx}$, vt sit $dZ$
$=Mdx+Ndy+Pdp$, tum, vt $\int Zdx$ fiat maxi-
mum vel minimum, vtique necesse est, sit $N-\frac{dP}{dx}=0$.
Verum quia haec aequatio est differentialis, atque adeo
differentio-differentialis, si functio $P$ ipsam quantita-
tem $p=\frac{dy}{dx}$ inuoluat, integratio eius vnam vel duas
constantes arbitrarias accipiet, neque propterea relatio
inter $x$ et $y$ penitus determinabitur. Obseruaui igitur
iam

MAXIMORVM ET MINIMORVM. 111

iam in meo tractatu, hanc relationem maximo mini-
mo ve conuenientem ita praeterea ad lubitum definiri
posse, vt, posito $x=a$, altera variabilis $y$ datum va-
lorem obtineat; ac si illa aequatio $N-\frac{dP}{dx}=0$ fuerit
differentialis secundi gradus, insuper vnam determinatio-
nem arbitrio nostro relinqui. His igitur casibus condi-
tioni maximi vel minimi adhuc alia conditio, ad valo-
res extremos ipsius $y$ pertinens, adiungi potest.

XXVIII.

Porro igitur quaeri potest, cum his casibus re-
latio inter $x$ et $y$ non penitus determinetur, eaque ad-
huc infinitis modis exhiberi queat, quinam prae omni-
bus reliquis maximum minimum ve producat. Hoc ve-
ro colligere poterimus ex parte incrementi absoluta ante
neglecta, quae hoc casu est $P\delta y$; cuius igitur valor,
quem induit posito $x=a$, etiam euanescere debet.
Atque hinc in genere intelligimus, si $\int Zdx$ debeat esse
maximum vel minimum, existente $dZ=Mdx+Ndy$
$+Pdp+Qdq+Rdr+Sds$ etc. aequationem
$N-\frac{dP}{dx}+\frac{ddQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3R}{dx^3}+\frac{d^4S}{dx^4}-$etc. $=0$, ita vlterius de-
terminari debere, vt, posito $x=a$, sequentibus satisfiat
aequationibus:

$P-\frac{dQ}{dx}+\frac{ddR}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3S}{dx^3}+$etc. $=0$
$Q-\frac{dR}{dx}+\frac{ddS}{dx^2}-$etc. $=0$
$R-\frac{dS}{dx}+$etc. $=0$; $S=0$ etc.

items.english: And it is manifest that in this case the absolute parts vanish of themselves, and so the problem is completely solved as soon as we set N = 0.

items.quote: Ita si $(bb-nxy+\frac{y^3}{c})dx$ debeat esse maximum vel minimum, ob $N=-nx+\frac{3yy}{c}$, quaestioni satisfit, statuendo $yy=\frac{1}{3}ncx$
items.english: Thus if (bb − nxy + y^3/c)dx must be a maximum or minimum, then since N = −nx + 3yy/c, the question is satisfied by setting yy = (1/3)ncx.

items.quote: integratio eius vnam vel duas constantes arbitrarias accipiet, neque propterea relatio inter $x$ et $y$ penitus determinabitur.
items.english: Its integration will receive one or two arbitrary constants, and therefore the relation between x and y will not be completely determined.

items.quote: Porro igitur quaeri potest, cum his casibus relatio inter $x$ et $y$ non penitus determinetur, eaque adhuc infinitis modis exhiberi queat, quinam prae omnibus reliquis maximum minimum ve producat.
items.english: It may further be asked, since in these cases the relation between x and y is not completely determined and can still be expressed in infinitely many ways, which one, above all the others, produces the maximum or minimum.
